title: Integrity baseline directory is stale v1.1 content carried unchanged into the v1.2 package
expected: A v1.2 package should carry an integrity baseline describing the v1.2 target, with every sidecar entry resolvable inside the delivered package
observed: INITIAL_SOURCE_SHA256.txt lists 2 entries; 1 resolves and 1 (01_manuscript/PAPER_II_preprint_draft_v1.1.md) is absent from the v1.2 package, so sha256sum -c reports FAILED open or read for it. README.md states 'Pending for v1.1' and refers to historical manifests 'under superseded/', but the v1.2 package contains no superseded/ path. INITIALIZATION_DIFF.md documents initialization of the v1.1 manuscript from the v1.1.5 intake, not the v1.1 to v1.2 transition.
impact: Protocol 4.1 requires all supplied sidecars to verify by content; this one cannot. No documented semantic diff exists for the v1.1 to v1.2 transition, so the scope of the v1.2 corrections is not evidenced inside the package. These are 3 of only 3 non-verifying sidecars out of 82 checked across the three packages. Does not affect the mathematics. Independently found by both the primary auditor and the adversarial challenger.
reproduction: From the package root: sha256sum -c 04_integrity/INITIAL_SOURCE_SHA256.txt ; ls for a superseded/ directory ; read INITIALIZATION_DIFF.md and compare its stated scope with the v1.2 target
proposed_disposition: Regenerate 04_integrity for the v1.2 baseline and supply a v1.1 to v1.2 initialization diff, or state explicitly that the directory is a retained historical v1.1 record

title: The official Erdos Problems page for #81 could not be retrieved directly
expected: Direct retrieval of the cited problem page
observed: https://www.erdosproblems.com/81 and every other path tried returned HTTP 403 to this auditor. The substantive status claim (the problem is open) is independently corroborated by the verified primary source [1], whose abstract states 'It is unknown whether this many cliques will always suffice.'
impact: Auditor-capability limitation, not a manuscript defect. Recorded because protocol 5.5 requires the current problem status to be verified separately.
proposed_disposition: No manuscript change required; confirm the page status by other means before release
